---
title: "Getting Started"
description: "Quick guide to using eoread for reading satellite products as xarray Datasets"
---

## Installation

Install eoread from the HYGEOS package index:

```bash
hyp add --hygeos eoread
```

## Core Concept

A reader is a **class**, one per (sensor, level), grouped by sensor under `eoread.readers`. Calling it reads the product and returns a lazy `xarray.Dataset` directly — nothing is read from disk or computed at construction:

```python
from eoread.readers.msi import Level1C_MSI

# Returns a lazy xarray.Dataset — nothing is read from disk yet
ds = Level1C_MSI("S2B_MSIL1C_20250320T104639_N0511_R051_T31UDS_20250320T142408.SAFE",
                 chunks=1000, resolution=60)
print(ds)
```

Every reader shares the base signature and may add reader-specific options as
extra keyword arguments with defaults:

```python
Reader(path, chunks=None, metadata_template=None, verbose=False)
```

Every returned dataset conforms to the canonical output schema and is validated
at read time (stamped with a `schema_version` attribute). Unsupported product
types or versions raise a `ProductError` subclass loudly — never a silent
fallback.

## Reading Products

### Sensor-Specific Readers

```python
from eoread.readers.msi import Level1C_MSI, Level2A_MSI
from eoread.readers.olci import Level1_OLCI, Level2_OLCI
from eoread.readers.meris import Level1_MERIS
from eoread.readers.oli import Level1_OLI
from eoread.readers.modis import Level1B_MODIS
from eoread.readers.ecostress import Level1C_ECOSTRESS, Level1B_ECOSTRESS, Level2_ECOSTRESS
from eoread.readers.pace import Level1B_PACE_OCI
from eoread.readers.venus import Level1C_VENUS, Level2A_VENUS
from eoread.readers.sgli import Level1B_SGLI
from eoread.readers.hypso import Level1B_HYPSO
from eoread.readers.goesng import Level1B_GOESNG
from eoread.readers.geosat import Level1_GEOSAT
from eoread.readers.pleiades import Level1_PLEIADES
from eoread.readers.pleiades_neo import Level1_PNEO
from eoread.readers.planetscope import Level1_PLANETSCOPE
from eoread.readers.hico import Level1B_HICO
from eoread.readers.prisma import Level1_PRISMA
```

`eoread.reader.discover_readers()` lists every reader class programmatically.

## Dataset Variables

All readers emit the canonical variable names from the `core.geo.naming` registry, on the canonical spatial dimensions `y` (rows) and `x` (columns):

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `Ltoa` | Top-of-atmosphere radiance (primary payload of MSI L1C, MERIS, …) |
| `Rtoa` | Top-of-atmosphere reflectance (primary payload of OLCI L2, OLI, VENµS L1C, …) |
| `BT` | Brightness temperature (thermal payloads) |
| `LST` | Land surface temperature (ECOSTRESS LSTE; single-layer, no bands dim) |
| `lat`, `lon` | Latitude/longitude rasters |
| `sza`, `saa` | Solar zenith and azimuth angles |
| `vza`, `vaa` | View zenith and azimuth angles |
| `cwav` | Central wavelength per band (nm), on the `bands` coordinate |

Angle variables may be emitted on a coarse tie-point grid with a `_tie` suffix
(e.g. MODIS keeps the raw 25 km tie grids). Multi-resolution products carry a
`bands_group` coordinate identifying each band's native resolution block.

Exactly one payload variable is the declared primary per reader class; the rest
are extras. No pre-decoded flag masks are stored (see [Quality Flags](#quality-flags)).

### Example: Inspecting a Dataset

```python
ds = Level1C_MSI("S2B_MSIL1C_...SAFE", chunks=1000, resolution=60)

print(ds.data_vars)
print(ds.coords)
print(ds.attrs["metadata"])
```

## Chunking

All readers accept a `chunks` parameter to control the spatial block size for dask (each reader carries a sensible per-sensor default):

```python
# Square chunks of 500 pixels
ds = Level1C_MSI("product.SAFE", chunks=500)

# Different chunk sizes for rows and columns
ds = Level1C_MSI("product.SAFE", chunks=(1000, 500))
```

> **Tip:** Do NOT chunk and then sel — this leads to very poor efficiency. Subset first, and set chunking as late as possible.

## Subsetting

Since eoread returns standard `xarray.Dataset` objects, you can use all of xarray's subsetting capabilities:

```python
# Subset by row/column indices (canonical dim names)
sub = ds.isel(y=slice(500, 1500), x=slice(400, 1400))

# Subset by coordinate values
sub = ds.sel(lat=slice(45.5, 46.0), lon=slice(3.0, 3.5))
```

You can also use helper functions from the `core` package for geographic subsetting:

```python
from core.tools import sub_rect, sub_pt

# Subset by bounding box (lat/lon in degrees)
sub = sub_rect(ds, lat_min=45.0, lon_min=3.0, lat_max=46.0, lon_max=4.0)

# Subset by center point and radius (radius in km)
sub = sub_pt(ds, pt_lat=45.5, pt_lon=3.5, rad=10)
```

## Quality Flags

No pre-decoded flag masks are stored in the dataset. Readers that support flags
advertise themselves through `ds.attrs['_flag_reader']` and decode boolean
masks on demand from the raw flag layers:

```python
from eoread.flags import GenericFlags

# lazy boolean mask of invalid pixels (MSI)
invalid = Level1C_MSI.getflag(ds, GenericFlags.L1_INVALID)
```

The supported flags vary by reader; `getflag` raises `ValueError` for an
unsupported flag name. To pack several flags into a single variable for
blockwise processing:

```python
from eoread.flags import FlagsInit, GenericFlags

init = FlagsInit(
    flags={GenericFlags.LAND: 1 << 0, GenericFlags.CLOUD: 1 << 1},
    dtype="uint16",
    flag_reader=ds.attrs["_flag_reader"],
)
ds = init.map_blocks(ds)   # adds a packed 'flags' variable
```

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `LAND` | Land/water mask |
| `CLOUD` | Cloud detection |
| `L1_INVALID` | Invalid L1 pixels |
| `L1_DEGRADED` | Degraded quality pixels |

## Metadata Filtering

By default, readers include the full product metadata in `ds.attrs['metadata']`. To reduce memory usage, you can filter it:

```python
# Only specific metadata branches (nested key paths)
ds = Level1C_MSI("product.SAFE", metadata_template=[
    ["General_Info", "Product_Info"],
    ["Product_Identifier"]
])
```

## Computing Results and Output

Data is loaded lazily. To trigger computation:

```python
# Compute a single variable
ltoa_values = ds.Ltoa.compute()

# Write to NetCDF (triggers computation automatically)
ds.to_netcdf("output.nc")
```

The `core.files.to_netcdf` helper adds automatic file naming, temporary files
and compression.

## Sample Products

Reader classes declare which sample products they support; `get_sample` resolves
one of them to an existing path (loud `FileNotFoundError` when none is available):

```python
from eoread.readers.msi import Level1C_MSI

path = Level1C_MSI.get_sample()          # first resolvable declared sample
ds = Level1C_MSI(path)

path = Level1_OLCI.get_sample("OLCI_L2_WFR")   # or select an explicit ID
```

The test suite runs on these real products only, and skips cleanly when a sample
is not available.

Some samples are also registered as downloadable from their provider: when the
local path is missing, `get_sample` fetches the product through SAND into the
local cache (`~/.cache/eoread/samples`) and resolves it from there — install
the `samples` extra to enable this. A failed download degrades to the same loud
error as a missing sample.

## Migrating from v1

The pre-v2 readers (`eoread.legacy.*`) and their `Level1()`/`Level2()`
auto-detection functions were removed in 2.0. To map a v2 dataset back to the
v1 layout (variable renames and reorganization), use the compatibility
transform:

```python
from eoread.compat import v1
ds_v1 = v1(ds)
```

A few sensors carry documented **clean breaks** where v2 values intentionally
differ from legacy (e.g. MODIS radiance formula, OLI solar correction); for
those, `v1()` raises with the explanation — see `eoread.compat.CLEAN_BREAKS`.
